catalog_quote: 2.1 Word-level stress. Two kinds of syllables, major and minor syllables, occur in Geba. Major syllables can consist of a complex onset and nucleus. [CCV]. Minor syllables can only consist of [CV]. A Geba word is a sequence of phonological syllables, one of which has the primary stress. In citation form, the first major syllable is stressed and wordinitial minor syllables are never stressed. In (1), the stress is found on the first syllable major syllable. (1) 'l̥á wóʔ thunder. In (2), the stress occurs on the second syllable but the first syllable is a minor syllable. (2) ə̄.'sʰùʔ feather. All monosyllabic words and grammatical particles are stressed but sometimes sentence and phrasal intonation may change this. ... 2.2.2 Minor syllables. audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding quotation, examples and all three locators (sec. 2.1 pp. 21-22, sec. 2.2.2 pp. 23-24, sec. 2.6 p. 36) are verbatim in the extracted text we hold of Shee 2008. (2) Deciding source: a 2008 first-hand descriptive grammar (MA thesis, xvii+263 pp), the sole grammar in Glottolog's bibliography for geba1237; its phonology chapter is brief and impressionistic but explicit about stress ('first major syllable is stressed; word-initial minor syllables never stressed; only major syllables carry stress'), which is exactly what the weight/left-edge, full-vs-reduced-vowel coding encodes. (3) Search for better sources (Glottolog langdoc: 3 refs; CiNii/TUFS; Shintani LSTCA list has no Geba volume) turned up only Kato 2008, downloaded and read: tonal vs atonic syllables, atonic never utterance-final, no stress-placement claim, hence silent/consistent. Minor nuance only: Kato's Leiktho a

sources.quote: No word-stress statement. Syllable C1(C2)V(ʔ)/T; three level tones (55, 33, 11) plus 軽声音節 'atonic syllables', written unmarked: 'Atonic syllables cannot occur utterance-finally. All vowels can appear in atonic syllables' (p. 172); 'at most two atonic syllables can occur in a row' (p. 216); pronominal proclitics jV/wV/nV/sV and the numeral 'one' tV~dV are always atonic with harmonizing vowel. This independently supports a tonal (full) vs toneless (reduced) syllable dichotomy consistent with Shee's major/minor split, though in the Leiktho dialect the reduced syllable is not restricted to schwa.
sources.locator: sec. 2 音韻 p. 172 (pdf p. 4); item 457-a note p. 216 (pdf p. 48); pronoun items 413-417 p. ~200 ('atonic' proclitic forms)
sources.note: Only other first-hand phonological description of Geba (Leiktho dialect); independent check on the major/minor (tonal/atonic) syllable dichotomy that our weight coding rests on. downloaded: silent on stress placement, consistent on reduced syllables.
